_doc: Thomas Harlan's cabin (#1126, Sean 2026-11-21): one room of hewn logs, worn and half fixed. Written by experiments/building_lab/homestead/gen_spec.py; FORMAT.md 'A log building's parts'.

identity.owner: Thomas Harlan, ex-army hospital steward, forties, alone
identity.trade: his homestead: he sleeps, cooks, washes and keeps his kit here; the claim's worth is the spring
identity.means: a man with a little saved: bought the place worn from its last owner this spring
identity.age_and_repair: the last owner raised it about 1874: the logs silver-grey, the chinking cracked and patched, the shakes curled; Harlan has started on it (a new log at the east wall's foot, a patch of new shakes) and left the rest for later: a patch of shakes missing, a porch board sprung, a rotten step
clues: his army trunk at the bed's foot
a shaving mirror and basin on the porch
boards and shakes bought and stacked in the barn
a new pale log among grey ones

lot._doc: Placed by the site (config/buildings/harlan_homestead.json) on the harlan_homestead pad (valley.json), its door gable to the yard (north).

levels._doc: One storey: the floor a step up on the sills, nine courses of logs to the plate (2.4 m clear), the loft's joists on the side walls' top logs, a 10/12 roof gabled front to back, its rakes 0.35 m past the gables.

frame._doc: Hewn logs on hewn sills on a fieldstone footing; the floor's joists between the sills on a girder down the middle; the loft's joists across on the side walls' top logs; common rafters on them, skip sheathing, split shakes.

foundation._doc: dry fieldstone under the sills, a foot into the ground

sill._doc: hewn sill logs, the front and back's through the corners

log_wall._doc: LogWall (src/structures/log_wall.gd): 6 1/2 in hewn faces, 9 in logs, 2 1/2 in of lime chinking (whitewash pale) set 1/2 in back, the ends 5 1/2 in past the corners

joist._doc: 2x6 at 24 in, 7 ft spans either side of the girder

ceiling_joist._doc: hewn 4 x 9 in at 16 in on the side walls' top logs, each spiked to a rafter's foot

floors._doc: the loft over the room on the side walls' top logs: its boards the room's ceiling (storage; a ladder later)

shakes._doc: split pine shakes, 10 in to the weather, on 1x6 boards a foot apart; the patch he's started round the hole

walls._doc: the chimney gable (east): the stone chimney outside it, the stove against it
the west gable: the woodpile against it
the door's long side (Sean, 2026-11-21: the door on the long side, under the eave), to the yard and the lane (north): the door, a small window either side, the porch
the back long side (south): its window over the trunk; a new log at its foot (Harlan's first repair)

side_porch._doc: the porch along the door's long side, a step down from the floor, its shed roof on three hewn posts under the main roof's eave

stairs._doc: three plank steps from the yard up to the porch before the door

list._doc: rough fieldstone up the outside of the east gable, the stove's pipe in through the logs

hung._doc: his shaving mirror on a nail beside the west window, over the washstand

rooms.use: he sleeps, cooks, eats and keeps his kit in the one room

use_points._doc: the bed the save uses (sleeping, later)
the clear spot beside the bed: where you stand to lie down
at his army trunk (the steward's kit, the photograph: later)
at the basin on the porch (washing the blood off: later)

H1.use: bed: its head against the west gable, in the back corner from the door
his army trunk at the bed's foot
under the window by the door, clear of its leaf
on the porch, under the mirror

repairs.what: a patch of shakes off the west slope over the bed (the boards show; it lets the rain in)
repairs._doc: shakes.missing's patch: no members; the fix lays them (the bundles in the barn)

repairs.what: a porch board sprung up at one end
the bottom porch step rotten through and broken

wear._why: one man, a few months, careful; the last owner's eight years under it

logs._why: hewn pine gone silver-grey (R1 a few years: old read near black on the logs, round 0) until a hewn-log entry is judged

new_wood._why: what Harlan has put in: pale and new

floor._why: rough wide pine boards (the recipe's rough class)

sources: C. A. Weslager, The Log Cabin in America (1969): hewn logs, chinking and daubing, openings sawn and bucked, shake roofs on skip boards.
Fred Kniffen and Henry Glassie, 'Building in Wood in the Eastern United States' (Geographical Review, 1966): corner timbering, hewn logs.
Fred T. Hodgson, Practical Carpentry (1883): common rafters, shingle lath.
USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook (FPL-GTR-282, 2021): spans.
